jobs.title: Director, Business Technology & Transformation
jobs.description:
North America Construction (1993) Ltd. – NAC Constructors Ltd. (NAC) is well known for our expertise in water and wastewater construction across Canada. Our self-performing team of almost 500 skilled professionals and experts in trades and engineering, comprehensively handles projects, from conceptualization to delivery. We also have extensive experience in fields such as civil, structural, process mechanical, building mechanical, electrical and instrumentation work. At NAC, our priority is to maintain the highest level of quality and safety. The depth of our resources is evident in the variety of projects we construct; from water filtration to wastewater treatment; dams to ethanol; we build it all….and more!

Bring your construction industry knowledge and technology leadership experience to NAC, where you’ll have the opportunity to shape our technology strategy, modernize business systems, and drive meaningful business transformation.

North America Construction (NAC) is looking for a business-minded technology leader who understands the demands of a construction or project-based environment and can translate technology into practical business improvements.

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Services, you will lead NAC’s technology strategy, manage a small internal technology team, and oversee external providers. Working closely with executive leadership and teams across finance, operations, estimating, HR, equipment, and projects, you will improve business systems, decision-making, productivity, and the employee experience.

Position Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Governance

Maintain a technology and transformation roadmap aligned with corporate priorities and business objectives.
Establish technology governance, standards, policies and decision-making processes.
Manage budgets and investment plans, assess emerging technologies, and develop and present business cases to executive leadership.

Enterprise Applications

Provide strategic direction for NAC’s enterprise applications, including ERP platforms, Jonas Construction Software, Procore, Primavera P6, Concur, HR systems, equipment and fleet systems, and future applications.
Lead or oversee enterprise system implementations, integrations, modernization and enhancements, including requirements definition, vendor management, implementation planning, change management and user adoption. Ensure systems are effectively integrated, aligned with business processes, and support operational efficiency and NAC's evolving business needs.

Data & Analytics

Lead data governance, stewardship, business intelligence and reporting capabilities, including Power BI, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs, and data warehouse and reporting architecture.
Ensure teams have access to reliable, timely and actionable information to support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.

Digital Workplace, Automation & AI

Lead digital workplace strategy, governance, and adoption across Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Teams, Power Platform, and Copilot.
Lead the planning, governance and adoption of AI and emerging technologies, including Microsoft Copilot, workflow automation, knowledge management and collaboration tools. Identify opportunities to improve productivity and business efficiency through effective implementation, change management and employee adoption.

Business Transformation & Process Improvement

Partner with business leaders to identify, prioritize and lead company-wide transformation initiatives and technology-enabled process improvements.
Lead initiatives to simplify workflows, reduce manual and administrative effort, and improve productivity and operational effectiveness. Work with business leaders to establish, measure, and evaluate the benefits and outcomes of these initiatives.

Technology Operations, Cybersecurity & Team Leadership

Provide strategic oversight of technology operations, infrastructure planning, managed service providers, service levels, cybersecurity, technology risk, business continuity and disaster recovery. Ensure technology services are secure, reliable and aligned with business needs and NAC's growth.
Lead and manage NAC's internal technology team, establishing priorities, delegating responsibilities, coaching and developing team members, and ensuring effective coordination with external service providers.
Ensure NAC has the appropriate resources, expertise, governance and controls to support its technology environment. Maintain overall accountability for technology performance, service delivery, operational reliability and risk management, whether delivered internally or through external providers.

Qualifications:

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline preferred. Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience will be considered.
Relevant professional certifications in project management, business analysis, IT service management, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture or organizational change management are considered assets.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology leadership, business systems, enterprise applications, digital transformation or business technology, with increasing responsibility for strategy, delivery and organizational outcomes.
Demonstrated experience leading technology functions, internal teams, external service providers and enterprise-wide initiatives.
Experience in construction, engineering, infrastructure, manufacturing or other project-based organizations strongly preferred.
Proven experience developing and executing enterprise technology strategies, roadmaps, governance frameworks and investment plans aligned with business objectives.
Demonstrated experience leading ERP implementations, enterprise application modernization, system integrations and business systems optimization.
Strong understanding of enterprise architecture, data management, business intelligence, analytics and executive reporting.
Experience leading enterprise business intelligence, data visualization and analytics platforms, such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, Qlik, Domo or comparable solutions. Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise reporting frameworks, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs and data governance practices that support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.
Demonstrated success leading technology-enabled business transformation, process improvement and organizational change initiatives, with a focus on measurable business outcomes.
Experience overseeing IT operations, infrastructure, cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity and disaster recovery planning.
Familiarity with AI, automation, Microsoft Copilot and emerging technologies, including their practical business applications, governance considerations and organizational adoption.
Strong business acumen and financial awareness, with the ability to develop business cases, evaluate technology investments and assess their business value.
Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management and change leadership skills, including the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business recommendations and outcomes.

By the end of your first 24 months, you will have:

Established and implemented a clear enterprise technology and business transformation roadmap aligned with NAC's corporate priorities.
Strengthened technology governance, investment planning and executive decision-making, while building strong business-wide relationships.
Improved the effectiveness, integration and adoption of key enterprise applications and advanced the modernization of NAC's business systems.
Expanded adoption of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Platform and Copilot, supported by appropriate governance and employee adoption.
Strengthened company-wide reporting, analytics, data governance and executive visibility into business performance.
Identified and delivered meaningful improvements through automation, workflow redesign and technology-enabled process transformation.
Strengthened cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity, disaster recovery and overall operational reliability.
Established a well-managed technology function with clear accountability, effective external partnerships and the capabilities required to support NAC's future growth.

NAC Offers:

Competitive compensation
Opportunities for career growth, development and advancement, including financial assistance
Comprehensive benefit plan (dental, vision, health, etc.)
Employee & Family Assistance Program
Excellent company matched pension plan
Registered Retirement Savings Plans
Additional time off between Christmas and New Year’s Day
Community involvement opportunities
Friendly working environment
Numerous team activities and various company events

NAC is committed to providing equal opportunities for all individuals to achieve their goals. If you feel that you need accommodations during the recruitment and selection process because of illness/disability, please contact Human Resources for further information

jobs.description:
Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Location:
Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.

What You'll Be Doing

CIBC Wealth Marketing is focused on strengthening our brand, deepening client relationships, and driving meaningful growth across our digital ecosystems. As AVP, Marketing Discoverability and Owned Channels, you'll shape and lead the organic channel strategy across social media, CIBC Wealth pre-login channels, and our content management system to increase brand visibility, customer engagement, and long-term client value. You'll act as the voice of the client by translating the needs of high-net-worth clients, prospects, and Investment Advisors into relevant channel, content, and media strategies that build authority and trust. You’ll define and execute enterprise-leading search strategies across search engine optimization, answer engine optimization, and generative engine optimization, while partnering with product, engineering, and content teams to strengthen website architecture, technical performance, and discoverability. You’ll also lead agency partnerships across media and creative, optimize marketing technology and innovation capabilities, and drive integrated planning across Canada, the United States, Wealth, and enterprise teams to deliver aligned, high-impact marketing initiatives. Throughout it all, you’ll continuously improve customer journeys from first interaction through conversion, retention, and cross-sell opportunities using a data-driven, results-focused approach.

CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview .

How You'll Succeed

People leadership and Strategic direction- Lead a high-performing team with deep knowledge of the Wealth landscape to ensure a strong understanding of business objectives, strategic direction, and the strategies required to deliver key business outcomes and key performance indicators. Set clear priorities, translate senior leadership direction into actionable plans, and oversee the management and continuous improvement of Marketing operational processes. Lead cross-functional CIBC Wealth teams to support strong execution and alignment across initiatives.
Search, discoverability and emerging technology leadership- Own the overall search strategy across the evolving landscape of search engine optimization, answer engine optimization, and generative engine optimization to strengthen CIBC’s Wealth presence, authority, and growth strategies within Canada. Lead strategy and execution across all pre-sign-on Wealth pages, including technical search engine optimization, keyword strategy, content optimization, metadata, tagging, and Core Web Vitals. Develop and lead the Wealth emerging technologies strategy with a clear focus on enhancing the client experience, while monitoring the evolving artificial intelligence search landscape and adapting discovery strategies to keep pace with market changes.
Media, Agency and Advisory expertise- Develop and lead Wealth agency models for creative development, media optimization, reporting, and operations, transforming historical ways of working to create greater agility, stronger responses to market events, and more effective positioning of the Wealth business. Manage agencies and external partners, analyze and optimize media plans and campaign performance, and provide consultation to Wealth Management brand and advertising managers on opportunities to increase traffic through online advertising, media, and search. Clearly communicate strategic recommendations, operating approaches, and investment rationale to partners and leaders.
Content, Thought leadership and Platform development- Lead the strategic plan, development, and roll-out of content and thought leadership programs across Global Asset Management, Private Wealth, Investor’s Edge, and enterprise partner initiatives. Build authority with the right audience segments through strong content strategies, including support for industry award positioning and brand credibility. Lead the development of new platforms, and the evolution of existing platforms, to meet the needs of clients and prospects, including overseeing new content management system capabilities that enable deeper segmentation, relevance, and personalization across all Wealth businesses.
Organic Social, Community and Influencer Discoverability- Lead Organic Social, Community, and Influencer Discoverability for Global Asset Management, Private Wealth, and Investor’s Edge, with accountability for the continuous improvement of Wealth-owned organic channels, including LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram, and websites. Develop platform-specific strategies that improve discoverability, engagement, and authority across social and community environments, and ensure creator and influencer activity is aligned with enterprise brand standards, compliance requirements, and business objectives.
Client Journey Optimization and Enterprise partnership - Act as a key contributor to client journey design, optimization, and implementation to improve how clients and prospects engage across channels. Serve as a subject matter expert when working with partners across Digital, Compliance, Customer Marketing, and other enterprise teams, bringing informed recommendations that strengthen execution and business results. Use your knowledge of Wealth businesses and marketing methodologies to drive growth, improve effectiveness, and enhance the client experience.

Who You Are

You have relevant experience. You bring 10-15 years of experience leading digital strategies, digital and mobile development, and content programs within complex organizations. You also have more than 10 years of experience in the Wealth or broader financial services business, with strong knowledge of the competitive landscape and client needs.
You can demonstrate experience in advertising agency leadership and management, digital strategy, content development, and business development solutions. It’s an asset if you bring experience supporting Wealth Marketing programs across multiple client segments and channels.
You’re a subject matter expert. You have first-hand working knowledge of retail brokerage or private banking front office environments. You also bring well-developed knowledge of content and business development solutions at a tactical level as they relate to the retail brokerage and Wealth Management business.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way and use insights to identify root causes, define key performance indicators, and recommend practical solutions.
You look beyond the moment. You work strategically with a strong understanding of business issues, processes, and outcomes as they relate to CIBC Private Wealth Management, Wood Gundy Investment Advisors, Private Banking, Trust, Private Investment Counsel, and our clients.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

The CFO will lead the transformation of the Company's finance function, establishing the financial infrastructure, systems, and processes required to support a multi-entity, acquisition-driven platform. At the heart of CSA Group is a vision: making the world a better, safer, more sustainable place. It's been part of our mission for nearly one hundred years: from the first engineering standard for railway bridges developed in 1919, to more than 3,500 standards, codes & related products today.

Our employees take pride in making a difference in people's lives through the work that we do. We're looking for people like you to help make it happen.

Job Summary

Responsible for leading treasury and cash flow management for the Canadian Standards Association (CSA), overseeing tax planning, administration, and compliance, and ensuring accurate accounting, reporting, and internal coordination related to CSA's investments and its interest in a separately governed investment entity.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Investment Reporting & Governance Coordination

Serve as liaison with the separately governed investment entity to ensure accurate accounting, reporting, and reconciliation of CSA's interest in, and transactions with, the investment entity.
For CSA’s investment portfolio, manage relationships with external investment consultants, asset managers, custodians, and banking partners.
Prepare and/or review investment-related account reconciliations, schedules and supporting documentation for monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting.
Coordinate with the investment entity, custodians, external investment managers, auditors and other service providers to obtain timely and accurate information required for CSA accounting and reporting.

Treasury, Cash Flow & Capital Management - Canadian Standards Association

Lead CSA's treasury operations and enterprise cash-flow management, including short- and medium-term liquidity forecasting.
Develop and maintain rolling cash-flow forecasts to ensure CSA has sufficient liquidity to meet operating, capital and strategic requirements.
Determine CSA's near-term funding needs and coordinate cash movements, contributions, distributions or other transfers with the investment entity in accordance with approved governance and authorization processes.
Manage CSA banking and treasury relationships, bank accounts, signing authorities and treasury controls.
Optimize CSA's operating cash balances and short-term liquidity within approved policies and risk parameters.
Develop liquidity management policies, cash reserve parameters and contingency funding plans for CSA.
Monitor counterparty exposure, interest rates, credit conditions and currency developments relevant to CSA's treasury activities.
Prepare treasury and liquidity reporting for executive management and the Board, including cash forecasts, liquidity headroom and key risks.

Tax Strategy, Planning, Administration & Compliance

Lead and coordinate CSA's tax planning, administration and compliance activities, working with external tax and legal advisors as appropriate.
Develop and maintain tax policies, internal controls and governance processes.
Assess tax implications of transactions between CSA and the investment entity, including investment income, distributions, capital movements, financing arrangements and restructurings.
Oversee corporate tax compliance, including income tax returns, information returns, withholding taxes, indirect taxes and applicable foreign reporting obligations.
Coordinate tax provisions and related financial statement reporting and audit support.
Monitor relevant Canadian and international tax developments and advise management on implications for CSA. Pension compliance
Lead the financial and regulatory compliance activities for CSA's Defined Benefit (DB) and Defined Contribution (DC) pension plans, ensuring adherence to applicable legislation, plan provisions, and regulatory requirements.
Oversee the financial administration of CSA's pension plans, including monitoring pension contributions, special payments, and funding obligations to ensure compliance with plan policies and regulatory requirements.
Work closely with Payroll, Human Resources, and external actuaries to validate pension calculations, contribution requirements, and funding transactions.
Monitor pension regulatory developments and funding requirements, including those established by the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), and advise management on implications for CSA.
Support pension-related accounting, financial reporting, audit requirements, and disclosures associated with CSA's pension obligations.

Preferred Education & Experience

University degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field; CPA designation strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in treasury, accounting/financial reporting and tax, ideally in a complex organization.
Strong experience in cash-flow forecasting, liquidity management, banking and treasury operations.
Experience accounting for investments and/or interests in separately governed entities and coordinating information from external managers, custodians or administrators.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, internal controls, corporate taxation and treasury governance.

Experience preparing materials for senior management and Boards or Board committees.
Critical and innovative problem-solving ability and strong attention to detail.
Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead across multiple finance disciplines and develop a high-performing team.

jobs.title: Director of Quality & Continuous Improvement
jobs.description:
Founded in 1991, the Mircom Group of Companies is North America’s largest independent designer, manufacturer and distributor of intelligent building and life safety solutions. Reaching customers in over 100 countries worldwide, our portfolio includes: fire detection & alarm, communications & security, mass notification, nurse call, and building automation & smart technologies.

Mircom’s mission is to save lives and protect property by providing a line-up of innovative and advanced solutions which are scalable to satisfy diverse user demands, from small buildings to the largest complexes. Our unwavering commitment to North American manufacturing enables us to offer the highest quality and best competitive value across our vast range of products and solutions.

Summary:

Mircom is seeking an experienced and dynamic Director of Quality & Continuous Improvement to lead and oversee all aspects of quality across the organization, including product design and development, manufacturing and testing, supply chain, sales, service, and corporate processes. Reporting directly to the President & CEO, this senior leadership role carries an enterprise-wide mandate to ensure that our products and services meet the highest quality standards and regulatory requirements. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in quality management, deep expertise in ISO standards and continuous improvement methodologies, and a strategic mindset to drive the company's quality objectives forward while fostering a culture of excellence throughout the organization.

Key Responsibilities:

Organizational Quality Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive quality management strategy that covers all facets of the organization, including product design, development, manufacturing, testing, sales, service, and corporate functions, with an unwavering emphasis on safety.
Maintain and continuously strengthen ISO 9001 compliance and maturity toward world-class quality standards, ensuring that quality practices align with organizational growth and Mircom's mission to deliver best-in-class solutions
Own and continuously mature the Quality Management System (QMS) across all departments to ensure a consistent, rigorous, and holistic approach to quality assurance.
Integrate Six Sigma, Lean, and other continuous improvement methodologies to systematically reduce defects and enhance overall product quality.
Support process improvement and automation initiatives to reduce variabilities and enhance manufacturing processes, anchored to key performance indicators including Cost of Poor Quality, Scrap Rate, First Pass Yield, Return Material Authorization rate, and Customer Satisfaction scores.

Leadership

Lead and manage the quality team, providing expert guidance on quality tools and techniques, mentorship, support, and training to ensure high performance and professional development.
Prepare and present clear, data-driven quality reports to the President & CEO and senior management, highlighting key performance indicators, quality improvement initiatives, and recommendations.
Manage and strengthen cross-functional relationships with stakeholders across product management, product development, operations and sales; serve as the voice of quality at the senior leadership level.
Challenge the status quo, negotiate quality objectives, and communicate progress toward continuous improvement goals with transparency and confidence.
Establish a framework for resolving quality-related problems quickly and efficiently, ensuring that root causes are rigorously addressed and preventive actions are systematically implemented.
Use data analytics to monitor key quality metrics, identify trends, and drive evidence-based continuous improvement initiatives.

People Development

Mentor and support team members to foster a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs to enhance team skills and knowledge in quality management, defect data analysis, root cause and corrective action (RCCA), and continuous improvement methodologies.
Invest in ongoing training programs for cross-functional staff to ensure adherence to quality standards and foster a sustained culture of continuous improvement.

Compliance

Ensure rigorous adherence to regulatory requirements and industry standards through comprehensive auditing processes, with a strong focus on ISO compliance.
Plan, execute, and oversee internal and external audits to assess compliance with quality standards and identify areas for improvement.
Develop and implement inspection and audit strategies to ensure comprehensive, systematic coverage of all manufacturing processes and quality management systems.
Address audit findings and implement structured corrective actions to resolve issues and prevent recurrence.
Implement robust risk management processes to identify and mitigate potential challenges in quality assurance, safety, and compliance efforts across the organization.

Continuous Improvement

Identify and execute continuous improvement, quality, and sustainability initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency across all functions.
Analyze quality data and metrics to identify trends, root causes, and areas for improvement.
Implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to address quality concerns and prevent recurrence.
Collaborate with product development and engineering teams to integrate quality into the design and development process from concept through launch, and participate in design reviews to ensure new products meet regulatory, customer, and Mircom quality standards

Supplier and Customer Relations

Develop and maintain strategic relationships with customers and suppliers to ensure that products and services consistently meet and exceed expectations and regulatory requirements.
Develop and manage supplier quality programs to ensure consistent material quality and component standards that support manufacturing excellence.
Ensure that customer quality concerns and feedback are addressed promptly and effectively.
Implement customer feedback loops to continually improve the quality of products and services.

Innovation and Technology Adoption

Stay abreast of emerging technologies relevant to the life safety and intelligent building systems industry, and evaluate their potential impact on quality management and product development.
Foster a culture of innovation by encouraging cross-functional collaboration between quality, product development, supply chain, manufacturing, field applications, and sales teams.

Requirements and Skills:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree (MBA, M.Eng., or M.Sc.) strongly preferred.
Minimum of 10–15 years of experience in quality management within a manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role.
Excellent leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate, mentor, and guide a diverse, high-performing team.
Proven experience developing and implementing quality management systems and processes across an entire organization, including product design, manufacturing, and corporate functions.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all departments and at the executive level.
Proficiency in quality management software and statistical analysis tools (e.g., Minitab, JMP, or equivalent).
Deep knowledge of ISO 9001:2015; proven experience managing certification, compliance, and audit programs.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and make data-driven decisions.
Demonstrated proficiency in Measurement System Evaluation (MSE), Design of Experiments (DoE), Failure Modes & Effects Analysis (FMEA), and predictive statistics.
Certification in Quality Management (e.g., Six Sigma, ASQ) is highly desirable.
Experience in a regulated, safety-critical industry (e.g., life safety, fire & security systems, building automation, electronics, aerospace, or medical devices) is a strong asset.
Professional accreditation in Quality Management or Quality Engineering is preferred.

What Mircom Offers:

A great working environment
Competitive salary
Group insurance benefits
Company RRSP program

jobs.title: Senior Director, Engineering - ICM
jobs.description:
About CaptivateIQ

CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize sales performance.

We started with incentive compensation management and are now expanding our platform to solve broader enterprise performance management challenges. Recognized by analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and G2 and backed by investors including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, and Sapphire Ventures, we help high-growth companies like Netflix, Figma, and Stripe drive revenue performance with flexibility and insight.

We’re building a category-defining platform at the intersection of finance, sales, operations, and AI. We’re looking for ambitious builders to help shape what comes next.

About The Role

As Senior Director of Engineering for Incentive Compensation Management (ICM), you’ll lead the engineering organization behind our flagship product that customers rely on to pay their teams accurately and motivate performance. You’ll lead managers across multiple teams and set the technical direction for making ICM AI-native without compromising the accuracy and trust our customers depend on.

This role combines product thinking, technical leadership, and organization building. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, GTM, and executive leadership to turn ambiguous opportunities into scalable products, and you’ll shape the engineering culture and structure that delivers them.

The Problems You’ll Solve

Making ICM AI-native. Decide where AI creates real customer value in plan design, calculation, and payout workflows, and build the quality and evaluation practices that make those features trustworthy.
Scaling a system where correctness is non-negotiable. Customers pay real people based on our calculations. You’ll balance speed of delivery with reliability, performance, and data integrity at enterprise scale.
Evolving the organization with the product. You’ll develop managers, clarify ownership, and adapt structure and process as the product matures.

What You'll Do

Set the strategy

Own the engineering strategy for ICM, aligned with company priorities, customer needs, and long-term platform direction
Identify new opportunities and guide product evolution, including the thoughtful application of AI to create differentiated customer workflows

Lead the organization

Recruit, grow, and inspire engineering managers and senior technical leaders
Build a culture of ownership, velocity, and continuous improvement
Design team structures and processes that evolve with product maturity

Raise the technical bar

Guide architecture decisions that balance speed, scalability, reliability, and maintainability
Stay close enough to the work to spot risks, challenge assumptions, and raise quality across the organization. You don’t need to write production code, but you do need to earn the respect of the engineers who do.

Drive execution

Create alignment and clear priorities across Engineering, Product, Design, and GTM
Make thoughtful tradeoffs and help teams move quickly while holding a high quality bar

What You'll Bring

15+ years of software engineering experience, including 6+ years leading managers and multi-team engineering organizations
A track record of building and scaling high-performing teams
Experience owning products end to end and scaling existing systems
Hands-on experience shipping AI/ML-powered product features, ideally LLM-based, including how you measure and maintain their quality. Experience applying AI to improve how engineering teams work is a plus.
Strong technical instincts across product architecture, infrastructure, reliability, and developer experience
A close partnership with Product and Design, and a focus on customer outcomes beyond engineering
The ability to create clarity for teams in fast-moving, ambiguous environments
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including experience working with executive leadership

Nice to have: Experience in enterprise B2B SaaS, finance or compensation systems, or other domains where calculation accuracy and auditability matter.

Why You'll Love This Role

You’ll own a flagship product in a category CaptivateIQ helped define and drive the next generation of AI-native capabilities
You’ll operate with significant ownership and influence across product and engineering strategy
You’ll work alongside deeply collaborative product, design, and engineering leaders
You’ll join a high-growth company with strong product-market fit and ambitious expansion plans
You’ll have the opportunity to shape not only products, but the engineering culture and organization that builds them

Benefits

Comprehensive Healthcare: 100% coverage for medical, dental, and vision for all FTEs, with roughly 75% coverage for dependents
Flexible Time Off: Flexible vacation days plus quarterly mental health days to ensure you have the space to recharge
Annual Stipends: Dedicated funds for your professional development and caretaking needs
Work Anniversary Bonuses: Annual bonuses to celebrate your milestones and contributions to the CaptivateIQ team that grow as your tenure does
Retirement Savings (US-Only): A 401(k) plan to help you invest in and secure your future
Premium Tools: The latest Apple hardware to empower you to do your best work
Inclusive Community: Active Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that celebrate shared identities and support our DEI goals by fostering an environment where diverse talent thrives

Notice to Prospective Candidates

Only emails from @captivateiq.com should be trusted
We are aware of active recruitment scams using the CaptivateIQ name, in which individuals pose as our recruiters and post fake remote job openings and make fake job offers on the Internet. Please note, we will never do the following:
Attempt to correspond with a candidate using a free web-based account, such as an email address that ends in @gmail.com, @yahoo.com, @hotmail.com, etc.
Make an offer of employment without conducting multiple rounds of interviews face-to-face using secure video-conferencing technology
Ask candidates to cash checks to buy equipment on behalf of CaptivateIQ
Ask candidates to make a payment in order to be considered for a position
Make early requests for candidates' personal information such as date of birth, passport details, credit card numbers, bank details and social security number, etc
Please note that we’ll only ask for more sensitive personal information in connection with background checks after an offer is made
Participate in an on-call rotation to provide after-hours support, ensuring timely resolution of critical issues and maintaining system uptime

CaptivateIQ participates in E-Verify, web-based system that allows enrolled employers to confirm the eligibility of their employees to work in the United States

About the faculty/service: Facilities

Facilities services are characterized by a dynamic and creative growing team where the winds of change are blowing, offering people like you opportunities to use your leadership and innovation skills to contribute to the achievement of their inspiring mission: to deliver best in class research infrastructure, reshape campus life and student experience, and provide a sustainable environment for students, researchers, teachers and community.

uOttawa’s facilities encompass three main sites that are comprised of over 600,000 square meters of building space (over 6.4 million square feet), 42.5 hectares of grounds, 125 buildings and 4,500 beds in 11 residences. There are over 150 employees in Facilities, including Project Managers, Energy and Commissioning Specialists, Mechanical and Electrical Engineers, Architects, and space Planners. The facilities capital and operating expenditures are in the range of $100M for the University’s $2.0 billion assets under management. The 20-year Capital spending plan envisions $4.0 billion of new investment highlighted by uOttawa launch of project Top Shelf, a $300 million capital investment to build a new facility for the Faculty of Health Sciences at uOttawa’s River Campus, as well as a tower at the Roger Guidon campus to house uOttawa’s new Advanced Medical Research Center (AMRC).

Position purpose:

Reporting to the Associate Vice-President, Facilities, the incumbent provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight of the University's facilities operations and maintenance activities to ensure the safe, reliable, efficient, and sustainable operation of its physical infrastructure in support of the University's teaching, research, and institutional objectives. Develops and implements strategies to drive operational excellence, organizational effectiveness, financial sustainability, and continuous improvement. Ensures the effective stewardship and lifecycle management of the University's physical assets through optimized resource utilization, risk-informed maintenance and infrastructure renewal strategies, while safeguarding operational resilience and business continuity.

In this role, your responsibilities will include:

Strategic Leadership and Operational Stewardship : Plans, directs, and oversees all aspects of the University's 24/7 facilities operations and maintenance programs, establishing strategic priorities, operational frameworks, and performance standards to ensure the effective stewardship of a physical asset portfolio valued at more than $3 billion. Ensures the delivery of safe, reliable, sustainable, and high-quality facilities services through effective governance, sound resource management, operational risk mitigation, and a commitment to institutional excellence and continuous improvement.
Operational Excellence and Service Delivery Optimization : Provides strategic leadership in the development, evaluation, and continuous optimization of facilities operations and maintenance service delivery models through performance benchmarking, reliability engineering, process improvement, resource optimization, and the implementation of industry best practices. Establishes comprehensive performance management frameworks, service standards, and key performance indicators to drive operational efficiency, accountability, service quality, and value for money, while ensuring alignment with the University's strategic and operational priorities.
Organizational Leadership, Workforce Effectiveness and Talent Development : Provides strategic leadership and direction to a diverse, multi-disciplinary, and multi-unionized workforce through the extended management team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. Ensures the effectiveness of organizational structures, workforce planning, succession management, leadership development, employee performance, and labour relations strategies to maintain a highly skilled, engaged, and adaptable workforce capable of meeting current and emerging institutional needs.
Critical Infrastructure Reliability and Continuity of Operations : Provides strategic oversight of the University's mission-critical infrastructure, building systems, central utility plants, and essential operational services to ensure their safe, reliable, efficient, and uninterrupted operation on a 24/7 basis. Establishes operational reliability standards, preventive and predictive maintenance strategies, system redundancy requirements, and contingency measures to minimize infrastructure failures, mitigate operational disruptions, and safeguard the continuity of teaching, research, and other essential University activities.
Regulatory Compliance, Occupational Health and Safety, and Operational Risk Management : Establishes and oversees comprehensive governance, risk management, and compliance frameworks to ensure facilities operations and maintenance activities meet applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, technical standards, and University policies. Provides strategic leadership in identifying, assessing, and mitigating operational, technical, environmental, and occupational health and safety risks, while fostering a proactive culture of regulatory compliance, workplace safety, and organizational accountability.
Financial Leadership and Resource Stewardship : Provides strategic leadership in the development, management, and optimization of the University's facilities operations and maintenance budgets, ensuring effective financial planning, resource allocation, expenditure control, and long-term financial sustainability. Establishes financial performance objectives and resource optimization strategies, evaluates operational investment opportunities, and ensures the efficient and responsible utilization of financial, human, and material resources in support of institutional priorities and service delivery requirements.
Emergency Preparedness, Infrastructure Resilience and Business Continuity : Provides strategic leadership in developing and implementing operational emergency preparedness, infrastructure resilience, and business continuity strategies to protect critical facilities and essential University services. Ensures the establishment, testing, and continuous improvement of emergency response procedures, infrastructure contingency plans, and operational recovery capabilities to minimize service disruptions and support the University's ability to respond effectively to emergencies, infrastructure failures, and other significant operational events.
Asset Lifecycle Management and Infrastructure Renewal : Provides strategic leadership in the assessment of infrastructure conditions, operational performance, asset reliability, and lifecycle maintenance requirements to support the sustainable management of the University's physical assets. Collaborates with institutional planning and capital investment stakeholders to identify, assess, and prioritize deferred maintenance, infrastructure renewal, and asset replacement requirements based on operational risk, asset criticality, lifecycle costs, and long-term institutional objectives.
Innovation, Digital Transformation and Operational Modernization : Leads the continuous modernization and transformation of facilities operations through the strategic evaluation and adoption of emerging technologies, digital asset management solutions, advanced building automation, predictive maintenance practices, and data-driven decision-making. Promotes innovation, process optimization, and organizational adaptability to enhance operational reliability, workforce productivity, service delivery effectiveness, and long-term operational sustainability.
Capital Project Integration and Operational Readiness : Provides strategic direction and oversight to ensure that operational requirements, lifecycle costs, asset maintainability, system reliability, and long-term sustainability considerations are effectively incorporated throughout all phases of capital projects, from initial planning and design through construction, commissioning, and project transition to operations. Collaborates with capital planning and project delivery teams to establish operational acceptance standards, ensure effective knowledge transfer, and facilitate the safe and efficient integration of new and renewed infrastructure into the University's ongoing operations and maintenance programs.
Institutional Collaboration, Executive Advisory and External Representation : Serves as a senior operational advisor to University leadership on matters relating to facilities operations, infrastructure performance, operational risks, resource requirements, and emerging industry developments. Establishes and maintains effective strategic relationships with academic and administrative leaders, research stakeholders, external partners, and professional associations to align facilities services with institutional priorities, promote service excellence, and represent the University's interests in relevant industry forums and professional networks.
Energy Management, Environmental Sustainability and Climate Resilience : Provides strategic leadership in the optimization of energy and utility management, the improvement of operational resource efficiency, and the integration of environmentally sustainable practices across the University's facilities operations. Collaborates with institutional sustainability and infrastructure planning stakeholders to advance energy conservation, greenhouse gas emissions reduction, climate adaptation, and long-term environmental performance objectives while maintaining operational reliability, service quality, and financial sustainability.

The Director, Enterprise Financial Management leads organization-wide financial consolidation, corporate accounting, financial governance and external reporting. Reporting to the Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk, this role establishes common accounting policies, timelines, standards and reporting requirements across all lines of business, and provides executive leadership to the Finance, Audit and Investment Committee, and the Board of Directors with a complete view of the organization’s financial position.

Reporting and leadership

Reports to the Vice President, Finance, IT and Risk.
Directly supervises 5-6 finance staff, including the Senior Manager, Payroll & Benefits, AP/Payments Manager and Senior Financial Analyst.
Provides organization-wide functional direction for budgeting, period close, audit preparation, journal-entry standards, financial controls and reporting requirements.

What you’ll be doing

Enterprise financial reporting and close

Lead the consolidated month-end and year-end close for YWCA BC and YW Housing Society, including organization-wide timelines, reporting standards, intercompany eliminations and review of submissions from line-of-business finance teams.
Prepare and review consolidated monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting for the VP Finance, executive leadership, the Finance, Audit and Investment Committee, and the Board.
Analyze organization-wide results, budget-to-actual variances, trends and emerging risks, and translate them into clear recommendations and an integrated financial narrative.
Establish organization-wide journal-entry standards and conduct risk-based reviews of entries to identify unusual transactions, inconsistent accounting treatment, control gaps and recurring errors.
Set accounting policies and reporting requirements for restricted contributions, deferred revenue, consolidation and other technically significant matters.

Budgeting, forecasting and financial sustainability

Lead the annual budget process and development of a multi-year forecast by establishing assumptions, timelines, standards, templates and system requirements.
Coordinate and review submissions from program-area Finance Directors, consolidate the final budget and forecast, and identify enterprise-wide surpluses, shortfalls, funding pressures and financial risks.
Review material business cases and pro formas for consistency with organization-wide assumptions, accounting policies, cash-flow requirements and long-term financial sustainability.

Audit, treasury and compliance

Plan and lead the external financial statement audit and other organization-wide assurance engagements, including auditor communications, information requests, proposed adjustments and significant findings.
Manage cash flow and oversee investments by monitoring balances, projecting liquidity needs and reviewing investment activity against policy.
Oversee Canadian charity and tax compliance, including GST, T3010, T4A and T5007 requirements, and support technically significant funder and government reporting matters.
Approve payments, credit card issuances and limit requests within delegated authority and organizational policy.

Systems, controls and continuous improvement

Administer finance-system governance, including the chart of accounts, financial dimensions, workflows, user access and approval structures; support effective integration with payroll and other enterprise systems.
Develop and improve finance policies, processes and internal controls, including segregation of duties, role-based access, audit trails and fraud-prevention measures.
Lead finance projects such as system enhancements, process automation and new program setup, with clear implementation, training and transition plans.
Investigate and resolve material discrepancies in accounts, reconciliations and reporting, and ensure corrective action prevents recurrence.

People leadership and collaboration

Lead, coach and develop the payroll, payments and financial analysis team through clear priorities, work review, performance management and development planning.
Partner with other Finance Directors and program leaders while maintaining clear accountability: program-specific analysis, budgeting, forecasting and funder reporting remain with the responsible line-of-business Finance Director.
Explain complex financial information clearly to executives, directors, managers, staff, auditors, funders, banks and external advisors, and resolve disagreements constructively.

Required education and experience

Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation and a bachelor’s degree in business, accounting or a related field.
9-11 years of progressively responsible financial management experience, including senior leadership responsibility in a complex, multi-program or multi-entity environment.
Strong knowledge of Canadian Accounting Standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations, including restricted contributions, deferred revenue, consolidation and intercompany accounting.
Demonstrated experience leading consolidated close, external audit, organization-wide budgeting and multi-year forecasting.
Experience supervising and developing a finance team, assigning and reviewing work, and managing performance.
Advanced financial systems and Excel capability; experience governing a modern cloud accounting system such as Sage Intacct is an asset.

Required capabilities

Sound independent judgment and the ability to design practical approaches where established guidance is limited.
Strong knowledge of internal controls, approval workflows, segregation of duties, fraud prevention and financial risk management.
Ability to build and test financial models, assess assumptions and communicate implications for cash flow and long-term sustainability.
Knowledge of Canadian charity and tax compliance, including T3010 and GST requirements; familiarity with T4A and T5007 reporting is an asset.
Executive-level communication skills, including the ability to present financial results and recommendations to senior leadership, Board committees and the Board.
Collaborative leadership style with the confidence to challenge assumptions, establish enterprise standards and support program-area teams.

jobs.title: Vice President of Finance
jobs.description:
About Stone Tile International

Stone Tile International Inc. (STI) is a national supplier of luxury natural stone, porcelain, slab and wood surfaces to designers, architects, builders and homeowners. Headquartered in Toronto with divisions in Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver, STI operates six product divisions (Stone Tile, Porcelain Tiles, 12MM, Stone Slabs, Wood and Gallery) through a network of showrooms, galleries and warehouses. STI is entering its next stage of growth and is building a finance leadership team to match.

The Role

This is a new role at STI, and a chance to transform how the business uses its numbers. The VP of Finance will tell STI’s financial story: what is driving results, where the opportunities and risks are, and what leaders should do next. You will build the data, metrics and AI-enabled tools that make that story fast and reliable, and use them to move the needle on margin, cash and growth across six product divisions and four regions.
You will own planning, forecasting, performance reporting, cash and financial controls, and lead the accounting function through the Director of Accounting. You will also be the first point of contact for contracts and legal matters, own IT infrastructure, oversee import compliance, and manage corporate insurance and governance, with guidance from the CFO. We are looking for a highly credentialed finance leader with real estate exposure, who is as comfortable in front of the executive team as in the data.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Storytelling and Insight

•    Turn financial results into a clear, compelling story for the President, CFO, executive team and ownership: what happened, why, and what to do about it.
•    Deliver a monthly management pack built around insight and action, not just tables of numbers.
•    Design visual dashboards that show performance by division, region, product and customer at a glance.
•    Lead monthly performance reviews with division and regional leaders and drive corrective action where results fall short.

Data, Metrics and AI-Enabled Finance

•    Define STI’s core financial and operating KPIs (margin, inventory turns, cash conversion, sales productivity, occupancy cost) and a single source of truth for each.
•    Build a modern finance data and reporting stack that connects ERP, sales and inventory data.
•    Identify and implement AI and automation across finance: forecasting, variance analysis, reporting, reconciliations and AP/AR, with sound controls.
•    Replace manual, spreadsheet-driven work so the team spends its time on analysis and decisions.

Financial Controls

•    Own STI’s financial control framework, including approval limits, segregation of duties and authorization of spend.
•    Review and challenge the internal controls designed and maintained by the Director of Accounting, and close gaps.
•    Ensure controls keep pace as processes are automated and new systems are introduced.

Planning and Forecasting

•    Own the annual budget process, delivering a board-ready budget before the fiscal year begins in April.
•    Build and maintain a rolling 12–18-month forecast by product division and by region.
•    Develop scenario and sensitivity models for volume, cost, margin, headcount and capital decisions.

Business Partnering and Margin Reporting

•    Act as the finance partner to sales, operations and division and regional leaders on margin, product mix and inventory.
•    Report on pricing and margin performance and help manage it, working with the Director, Supply Chain, who owns day-to-day pricing.

Import Compliance and Trade

•    Oversee compliance with regulations and administration for importing goods into Canada, including customs, duties and tariffs, with day-to-day administration by the Director of Accounting.
•    Monitor foreign trade policy, tariffs and geopolitical events, and model their impact on landed cost, sourcing, FX and margin.
•    Brief the CFO and executive team on trade risks and recommend responses.

Contracts and Legal

•    Own the review of contractual documents, such as purchase orders and contracts from general contractors, customer and vendor agreements, from a legal and business perspective, with guidance from the CFO.
•    Act as the first point of contact for general legal matters, resolving where appropriate and escalating to the CFO.

Cash, Working Capital and Treasury

•    Produce and manage a 13-week cash flow forecast and longer-range cash plan.
•    Set and manage targets for inventory, customer credit terms and collections.
•    Manage day-to-day banking, covenant monitoring and foreign exchange exposure, within CFO policy.

Real Estate and Capital Investment

•    Lead the financial analysis for real estate decisions: new or relocated showrooms and warehouses, lease renewals, lease versus buy, and occupancy cost by location.
•    Maintain a lease and property portfolio view, including commitments, renewal dates and occupancy costs as a share of revenue.
•    Build business cases for capital expenditures, new product lines and major hires, and track post-investment returns.

Insurance and Corporate Governance

•    Manage the corporate insurance program, including coverage reviews, renewals, claims and the broker relationship, within CFO direction.
•    Support corporate governance across STI’s entities, including corporate records, resolutions and annual filings.

IT Infrastructure and Support

•    Own IT infrastructure and support, including managed service providers, hardware and software, user support and cybersecurity, with guidance from the CFO.
•    Build a technology roadmap that supports finance transformation and the wider business.

Acquisitions

•    Lead financial due diligence on acquisition targets with the Director of Accounting, under the direction of the CFO.
•    Help integrate acquired businesses into STI’s reporting, controls, systems and processes.

Leadership and Transformation

•    Lead, coach and develop the Director of Accounting and build a finance team that is analytical, data-fluent and business-facing.
•    Set a finance transformation roadmap and deliver measurable improvements in speed, accuracy and insight.
•    Ensure a fast, reliable month-end close feeds planning and reporting.

Success in the First 12 Months

•    A monthly management pack and dashboards the executive team relies on to make decisions.
•    Agreed KPIs with one source of truth, reported consistently by division and region.
•    At least two AI or automation use cases live in finance, with time saved and accuracy gains measured.
•    An approved FY budget, rolling forecast and 13-week cash forecast in place and trusted.
•    Financial control framework reviewed, with gaps identified and closed.
•    A clear process for contract review and legal escalation, and a trade and tariff impact model in use.

Qualifications

•    CPA designation required; an MBA and/or CFA charter is a strong asset.
•    12+ years of progressive finance experience, including 5+ years leading FP&A, commercial finance or corporate finance at a senior level.
•    Exceptional financial storyteller: proven ability to present to executives, ownership and lenders and turn analysis into decisions.
•    Track record leading finance transformation, including data, BI/dashboard and automation or AI initiatives.
•    Strong data skills: modern BI tools (e.g., Power BI), advanced modelling, and comfort working with large data sets.
•    Experience reviewing commercial contracts (e.g., construction and general contractor agreements, purchase orders) from a legal and business perspective.
•    Knowledge of import regulations, customs and tariffs, with a strong grasp of foreign trade policy and geopolitical risk.
•    Experience overseeing financial controls, corporate insurance and IT infrastructure.
•    Real estate exposure: lease analysis, property investment or real estate finance, and lease accounting.
•    Acquisition due diligence and integration experience is an asset.
•    Public company or public sector experience is an asset.
•    Multi-location, multi-entity Canadian experience; distribution, wholesale, retail or building products experience is an asset.
•    French is an asset.

Working Conditions

•    Based at the Toronto head office, with some travel to Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver
•    Presents regularly to the executive team and external stakeholders
•    Extended hours during budget, year-end and audit periods as required

jobs.description:
⠀

The Director, Defense Portfolio Strategy reports to the Chief Strategy Officer and directly supports the CSO's enterprise mandate to identify and unlock growth above the underlying market rate. Defense is CAE's largest such opportunity, and this role carries the analytical and transactional workload behind it.

The Defense & Security business unit owns its strategy. This role does not duplicate or adjudicate it. Instead, the Director works on the questions that sit above and across the operating plan — where CAE should allocate capital and capability within the Defense domain, which adjacencies merit entry, what the enterprise should build, buy, or partner for, and how the Defense portfolio should evolve to deliver above-market growth.

The Director operates as a full member of the corporate strategy team. The above-market growth mandate is enterprise-wide and held by the CSO; this role brings dedicated defense-domain depth to it, working alongside colleagues whose expertise spans other domains and functions. Portfolio work remains collective — the addition here is capacity and depth against a specific CEO-level priority, not a redrawing of scope.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy and Capital Allocation

Quantify the gap between the Defense market's underlying growth rate and CAE's growth ambition, and maintain a live view of which portfolio moves close it — with what confidence, on what timeline, and at what capital cost.
Develop CAE's point of view on where Defense capital and capability should be deployed to generate above-market growth, and where they should not.
Assess portfolio adjacencies, capability gaps, and whitespace across the Defense domain, framing entry, expansion, and exit questions for executive decision.
Build the build / buy / partner logic for capabilities the Defense portfolio requires.
Contribute the Defense lens to enterprise portfolio reviews and capital allocation discussions alongside corporate strategy colleagues covering other domains.
Develop investment cases for new markets, segments, and capability plays, in partnership with the business unit strategy team.

M&A and Partnership Pipeline

In Collaboration With The Strategy Team Colleagues

Build and actively cultivate a pipeline of acquisition and partnership candidates aligned to the Defense portfolio thesis, maintaining live relationships well ahead of any formal process.
Maintain a standing view of the defense industrial landscape — who is consolidating, who is available, where valuations are moving.
Partner with Corporate Development through diligence and execution; support integration planning where strategic rationale must be preserved.
Evaluate teaming, joint venture, and partnership structures as alternatives to acquisition.

Technology Enabler Pipeline

Identify, map, and cultivate relationships with startup, scale-up, and pre-IPO companies whose technologies could accelerate CAE's Defense capabilities or threaten its positions.
Maintain an ongoing landscape view of emerging technologies relevant to simulation, training, and mission readiness.
Create structured pathways from early engagement through pilot, commercial partnership, investment, or acquisition.
Connect CAE to relevant venture, accelerator, and defense-innovation ecosystems, sharing that access across the strategy team.

Market Intelligence and Enterprise Contribution

Bring outside-in intelligence on defense budgets, procurement trends, geopolitical shifts, and competitor moves into both business unit and corporate strategy discussions.
Contribute to enterprise strategy work beyond Defense where domain insight is relevant — this is a shared-team role, not a single-vertical one.
Prepare executive-level analysis and briefing materials for the CEO, Executive Committee, and Board.
Support Government Relations and business unit leadership with strategic context for key customer engagements.

This Role Succeeds Through Partnership Rather Than Authority

With the Defense & Security business unit — the BU owns its strategy and operating plan. The Director brings portfolio and transaction perspective to that work and takes the BU's market reality into enterprise portfolio decisions. Joint work products, jointly presented.
With corporate strategy colleagues — a peer contributing defense depth to a shared team agenda, drawing on colleagues' functional and domain expertise in turn. Enterprise portfolio work remains collective.
With Corporate Development — origination and strategic framing from this role; transaction execution led by Corporate Development.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or postgraduate degree in Business, Strategy, Economics, Engineering, International Relations, or a related field; MBA an asset.
12+ years in corporate strategy, corporate development, management consulting, or defense/aerospace industry roles.
Demonstrated experience with portfolio strategy, capital allocation, or build/buy/partner decision-making in a complex global organization.
Strong command of defense markets, government procurement, and allied defense spending dynamics.
Direct experience with M&A origination, partnership development, or technology scouting.

Preferred Qualifications

Track record of earning influence without formal authority, and of working effectively as a peer within an established team.
Strong financial, analytical, and commercial judgement.
Comfortable operating with ambiguity, across multiple time horizons, in a fast-moving environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level presentation and narrative skill.
Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearances.

Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
