Job Description

What makes this role important at Ipsos?

As a Vice President, you will serve as a senior quantitative research leader and trusted advisor to clients. You will work with senior stakeholders to translate complex business challenges into clear learning agendas, testable hypotheses, and rigorous research methodologies that drive decision-making and business impact.

This role requires deep expertise in quantitative research design, advanced statistical techniques, and quantitative best practices. You must be comfortable thinking on your feet, providing methodological guidance in real time, and confidently defending analytical approaches with clients and colleagues. Beyond delivering insights, you will help shape the questions that matter, determine how they should be tested, and translate findings into strategic recommendations.

Our ideal candidate is an intellectually curious and commercially minded research leader who combines methodological excellence with strategic thinking, client advisory skills, and a passion for turning evidence into action.

This is a highly quantitative role. Candidates must possess significant hands-on experience designing, executing, and interpreting advanced quantitative research studies and analyses. Experience managing quantitative projects alone is not sufficient; successful candidates will have personally applied advanced analytical techniques and statistical methods throughout their careers. Individuals whose experience is primarily qualitative should not apply.

What You Can Expect To Be Doing

Lead the design of complex research and advisory engagements that address critical client business challenges and contribute to business growth.
Translate client issues and strategic questions into learning agendas, testable hypotheses, and robust research methodologies.
Apply advanced analytical techniques and methodological best practices to ensure research is insightful, innovative, and fit for purpose.
Serve as a senior advisor to clients, helping them interpret findings, evaluate strategic options, and make informed decisions.
Lead the development of reports, presentations, workshops, and executive-level recommendations that move beyond reporting results to driving action.
Collaborate across Ipsos service lines to bring the full breadth of Ipsos expertise to clients and identify opportunities for integrated solutions.
Contribute to business development activities, including proposal development, thought leadership, and identifying opportunities for growth within existing and prospective client relationships.
Build Ipsos' reputation internally and externally through subject matter expertise, innovation, thought leadership, and market presence.
Coach and mentor researchers at all levels on research design, analytical thinking, storytelling, strategic consulting, and client management.

Client Management Responsibilities

Acts as a senior trusted advisor to client leadership teams, providing strategic counsel on research, insight generation, and business decision-making.
Leads complex client conversations involving methodology, interpretation, business implications, and challenging or ambiguous situations.
Anticipates client needs and proactively recommends research and advisory solutions that address emerging opportunities and risks.
Builds and maintains senior-level relationships that contribute to long-term partnerships, business retention, and revenue growth.
Supports and coaches team members in managing client relationships and navigating difficult stakeholder situations.

Study Lead Responsibilities

Oversees the design and execution of complex research programs from hypothesis development through final recommendations.
Guides methodological decisions and analytical approaches, ensuring technical rigor and alignment with client objectives.
Leverages advanced quantitative techniques, segmentation, modeling, forecasting, and other analytical approaches, as appropriate.
Synthesizes findings across multiple data sources to identify patterns, implications, and strategic opportunities.
Leads development and delivery of executive-level reporting and presentations that connect research findings to business outcomes.

Employee Management Responsibilities

Manages and develops researchers and team leaders, providing ongoing coaching, mentorship, and performance development.
Builds team capabilities in research design, analytical methods, strategic thinking, consulting skills, and client advisory.
Creates an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, continuous learning, and methodological excellence.
Identifies and develops future leaders within the organization.

STRATEGIC THINKING EXPECTATIONS

Serves as a strategic leader for client accounts and research engagements.
Demonstrates hypothesis-driven thinking and the ability to connect business objectives with research solutions.
Quickly assesses complex situations, identifies key issues, and develops practical paths forward.
Balances methodological rigor, client realities, commercial considerations, and organizational priorities.
Anticipates emerging trends, risks, and opportunities and helps shape Ipsos' approach to addressing them.
Influences strategic direction for clients, projects, and the broader business through evidence-based recommendations and thought leadership.

This might be the job for you if you have:

8-10+ years of experience in market research, insights, consulting, or a related field.
Deep expertise in quantitative research methodologies and advanced analytical techniques.
Proven ability to transform complex business questions into actionable research programs and testable hypotheses.
Strong understanding of research best practices and the ability to select, defend, and communicate methodological approaches.
Exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to think on your feet in high-stakes client situations.
Demonstrated success advising senior client stakeholders and leading complex engagements.
Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to connect data to strategic business decisions.

SickKids Foundation, with over 50 years of philanthropic impact is Canada's largest charitable funder of child health research, learning and care, raising over $200 million last year. As a national charity, SickKids Foundation invests in national and international initiatives to benefit children in Canada and around the world. As the fundraising partner to The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids), we are aligned in supporting Precision Child Health (PCH), the future of tailoring medicine to each child's unique traits so SickKids can diagnose faster, treat smarter, and predict better.

We are driven by our core values of integrity, collaboration, excellence, innovation, and inclusion, with goals of delivering a superior donor experience, investing in our people and culture, driving innovative and sustainable fundraising, and disrupting the market through data and technology.

SickKids Foundation is committed to an inclusive culture by embedding equity, diversity and inclusion in our policies, practices, and behaviours. We aim to build awareness and skills in this area, both internally and with our partners. Our commitment extends to creating a safe, positive work environment. For details on our Equity, Diversity & Inclusion commitment, please click here.

We’re committed to attracting and retaining passionate individuals to help create a healthier future. That’s why SickKids Foundation is looking for a new Associate Director, Data Engineer.

Description Of The Position

Reporting to the Director, Data Science & Engineering, the Associate Director, Data Engineer designs, builds, and operates enterprise-grade data platforms that deliver trusted, well-governed data across SickKids Foundation. The role will help establish and evolve a production-grade cloud platform using medallion architecture principles, with a focus on reliability, data quality, cost efficiency, and scalable delivery.

As a senior hands-on technical contributor, you will set engineering standards, support platform incident response, enable self-serve analytics and AI-powered data products, and provide specialized technical guidance to data and analytics partners across the Foundation.

You will

Design, build, and operate enterprise-grade data engineering platforms using modern cloud technologies such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, and Databricks, aligned to bronze, silver, and gold medallion architecture principles.
Build and maintain robust, idempotent ETL/ELT pipelines with embedded validation, data quality checks, clear lineage, and repeatable delivery workflows.
Design data models and semantic layers that make trusted data accessible for analytics, reporting, and self-serve business intelligence.
Establish platform observability through query profiling, cost attribution, utilization metrics, alerting, and SLO/SLA monitoring; lead day-to-day response to data availability and performance incidents.
Define and enforce coding standards, CI/CD patterns, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices to support consistent, secure, and scalable platform deployment.
Partner with business stakeholders, Data & Analytics, IT/Infrastructure, and Security teams to translate requirements into reliable platform capabilities and support appropriate access, governance, and compliance.
Enable AI and advanced analytics use cases, including natural-language querying and AI-powered data products, by partnering with stakeholders to identify and deliver high-value opportunities.

Deep technical expertise with modern cloud data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, or Databricks and strong knowledge of medallion/lakehouse architecture.

Hands-on experience developing production-grade ETL/ELT pipelines and working with data quality, governance, CI/CD, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices.

Working knowledge of AI and advanced analytics tooling, including approaches that support natural-language querying and AI-powered data products.
Strong technical judgment, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical stakeholder groups.

new_jobs.title: VP Technology and Innovation Partners (Partnerships Ecosystem)
new_jobs.description:
Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

About The Opportunity

Dayforce is the AI-powered people platform. One platform for HR, Pay, Time, Talent, and Analytics, with AI built into how work gets done. Partners are central to that strategy. The AI capabilities, data, and solutions our partners bring to the platform extend what Dayforce AI can do for customers and accelerate how fast we grow.

That is changing what our technology ecosystem does for the business. Partners are moving from integrations that sit next to the platform to AI-enabled solutions we resell, transact, and build on together. That shift touches revenue, product strategy, and how Dayforce competes.

The VP, Technology and Innovation Partners owns the strategy, performance, and commercial outcomes of Dayforce’s technology partner ecosystem across five areas: ISV partners Dayforce resells, including Go1, Emburse, Docusign, Aquera, etc.; ISV partners with certified connectors on the Dayforce Exchange across Pay and Benefits and HR and Talent; the Microsoft partnership; In Country Payroll partners; and Dayforce Build.

This is a leader-of-leaders role with a number attached. You will be accountable for resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, marketplace revenue, and the quality of the integrations and solutions partners deliver. You will lead an established team of four senior leaders who own the Microsoft alliance, In Country Payroll, Pay and Benefits ISVs, and HR and Talent ISVs. You will operate as a peer to the leaders of our Services Delivery and Community pillars. We are looking for a leader with the commercial, go-to-market, and technology depth to run all of it as one business.

Work is what you do, not where you go. For this role, we are open to remote work and can hire anywhere in the US or Canada.

What You’ll Get To Do

Business Ownership and Growth

Carry the technology partner number. Own resell bookings, partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, and marketplace revenue, with clear accountability to the CRO organization.
Scale software resell. Grow attach of resold partner solutions to core Dayforce deals. Set the margins, pricing, packaging, and commercial terms that make resell a material, predictable revenue line.
Make the Exchange transactable. Share ownership with Product of moving the Dayforce Exchange from referral-only to transactable. Own the partner commercial model, partner onboarding, and partner readiness.
Make partners a growth engine for Dayforce AI. Build the partner strategy that extends the AI-powered people platform. Bring in the AI partners, agents, and solutions that deepen what Dayforce AI delivers for customers and create new revenue.
Own the portfolio. Decide which partners we resell, which we integrate and refer, which we co-build with, and which we retire. Close gaps in the Dayforce offering through build, partner, or buy recommendations with Product and Corporate Development.

Microsoft

Serve as executive sponsor for Microsoft, supporting the alliance lead who owns the day-to-day relationship across partnership, sales, and product teams.
Grow Dayforce’s position as a strategic HCM and payroll partner in the Microsoft ecosystem, across Azure, Dynamics 365, Copilot, and Teams.
Build and run a joint HCM, Pay, and ERP go-to-market with Microsoft and the SI partners that deliver it, including marketplace, co-sell programs, and field-to-field engagement.
Lead AI co-innovation that turns Microsoft technology into differentiated Dayforce AI capability.

Global Payroll and In-Country Partners

Own the strategy and performance of the In Country Payroll network that delivers and extends Dayforce global payroll.
Set standards for coverage, service quality, compliance, integration, and customer experience, and hold partners to them.
Rationalize and expand country coverage based on customer demand and deal pipeline.
Work with Product and Operations to deliver one consistent global payroll experience, whether Dayforce or a partner runs the payroll.

Dayforce Build

Dayforce Build is the platform customers and partners use to build integrations, extensions, and new capabilities on Dayforce. Partners are already building in it. This role turns that early momentum into a scaled partner ecosystem.

Own the partner strategy and growth of Dayforce Build, sharing ownership of the platform roadmap with Product and Engineering.
Move partner builds, including AI-powered extensions and agents, from proof of concept to production, certified, and in market.
Recruit and grow the ISVs, SIs, and developers building on the platform, including through the Dayforce Developer Community.
Connect what partners build to the Exchange, the resell program, and field go-to-market so builds turn into revenue.
Set quality, security, and certification standards for everything partners build on Dayforce.

GTM and Field Execution

Build repeatable joint go-to-market motions with priority partners: co-sell plays, joint campaigns, enablement, and account mapping.
Drive field adoption of resell and partner solutions across segments.
Equip Dayforce sellers with the positioning, pricing, and proof points to attach partner solutions to core deals, so partner attach is a default consideration rather than an exception.
Partner with Marketing on ecosystem launches, events, and partner showcases.

Leading the Team

You will lead four senior leaders, each running a distinct motion. Your first job is to make them operate as one ecosystem.

Microsoft Alliance owns the day-to-day Microsoft relationship, co-sell, and joint GTM.
In Country Payroll owns the global payroll partner network, coverage, and service quality.
Pay and Benefits ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce Pay and Benefits through connectors and resell.
HR and Talent ISVs owns the partners that extend Dayforce HR and Talent through connectors and resell.
Coach, develop, and raise the bar across the team. Have a clear point of view on strengths and gaps within your first quarter.
Establish one scorecard and operating rhythm across all five areas, balancing long-term platform strategy against near-term revenue.

Technology and Product Influence

Serve as the technical voice of the partner ecosystem inside Dayforce.
Partner with Product and Engineering on integration architecture, APIs, connector certification, and partner developer experience.
Partner with Product on the Dayforce AI roadmap, so partner AI capabilities complement and extend what Dayforce builds.
Scout emerging technology and AI partners that expand the Dayforce platform and create new revenue.

Executive and Cross-Functional Influence

Operate as a trusted counterpart to executive leadership across Sales, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and Finance.
Negotiate complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements, and hold partners accountable through data, not sentiment.
Present performance, risk, and opportunity directly to the executive team with clarity and conviction, including in forums with sponsor visibility.
Executive exposure to the CRO, Product, and Technology organizations, and to Microsoft executive leadership, as a matter of routine, not exception.

Skills And Experience We Value

15+ years in enterprise software, with at least 7 years leading technology partnerships, alliances, or ecosystem businesses, and meaningful time spent carrying a number.
A track record of growing partner revenue, including resell or OEM models, with specifics: bookings delivered, attach rates moved, marketplace revenue grown.
Direct experience scaling a SaaS marketplace, app ecosystem, or developer platform program, ideally including the move to a transactable model.
Deep experience with Microsoft or another hyperscaler: co-sell programs, marketplace, and executive sponsorship.
Strong commercial judgment. You have structured and negotiated complex resell, revenue share, and strategic partner agreements.
Enough technical depth to lead conversations on APIs, integration architecture, cloud platforms, and AI with engineering teams on both sides.
A clear point of view on how AI is reshaping software ecosystems, and experience bringing AI partners and solutions to market.
Experience leading senior leaders who each run a distinct business and making them operate as one team.
Familiarity with HCM, payroll, ERP, or an adjacent enterprise platform category.
Comfort operating in a private equity-backed environment, with the pace, transparency, and accountability that entails.
Highly analytical and metrics-driven, at ease in complex matrixed environments and in front of an executive audience.

What Would Make You Stand Out

Global payroll experience is a strong advantage.
Prior PE-backed experience is a strong advantage.

What’s In It For You

Dayforce is fueled by the diversity of our talented employees. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider and embrace ALL individuals and what makes them unique. We believe our employees should be happy and healthy, with peace of mind and a sense of fulfillment.

We encourage individuals to apply based on their passions.

Dayforce encourages personal and professional growth. We offer excellent time away from work programs, comprehensive wellness initiatives and recognition through competitive pay and benefits.

With a commitment to community impact, including volunteer days and our charity, Dayforce Cares we provide opportunities for you to thrive both in your career and personal life. Our focus is not just on your job but on supporting you to be the best version of yourself.

This job posting is for an existing vacancy

Artificial intelligence may be used in the screening, assessment, or selection of applicants for this position.

Dayforce is committed to providing accommodations for applicants with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. If you require an accommodation, please contact us at accessibilty@dayforce.com.

About The Salary Ranges

The final compensation offered may vary based on a variety of factors, including bonuses and/or incentives, or a candidate’s experience, skills, budget and location. Our company is committed to providing a fair, equitable, and competitive package that reflects the value an individual brings to the organization.

Proficiency in English is required for this position as this role will regularly interact with English-speaking stakeholders, co-workers, managers and/or clients across the world. Further, our back office support teams, including but not limited to Human Resources, are primarily English speaking. Please note: This is a hybrid role based in Toronto. Candidates outside Ontario would need to relocate to meet the role's in-office requirements.

About The Role

As Director, Technology Delivery Lead, you are accountable for the end-to-end technology delivery of Em, BMO InvestorLine's premier AI agent. You will lead the integrated delivery system across AI engineering, wealth platforms, Microsoft Azure, data, architecture, quality engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and third parties to deliver safe, resilient, scalable, and measurable client outcomes.

You will operate as the principal technology counterpart to the Product Owner for Em. Together, you are jointly accountable for overall delivery: the Product Owner leads product vision, client value, priorities, and acceptance; the Technology Delivery Lead owns the integrated technology plan, engineering execution, technical quality, production readiness, and predictable delivery. This role is not a program coordination position. It is a hands-on senior technology leadership role with clear decision rights and accountability for outcomes.

Mandate and Decision Rights

Own the integrated technology delivery plan for Em from discovery and architecture through build, evaluation, release, operation, and continuous improvement.
Jointly commit scope, sequencing, release outcomes, and delivery forecasts with the Product Owner, balancing client value, technical feasibility, risk, cost, and capacity.
Make or escalate timely technology delivery decisions across architecture, engineering, environments, data, integration, testing, controls, and production readiness.
Hold delivery teams and partners accountable for agreed outcomes, quality standards, dependencies, and evidence-based release criteria.
Protect the product from unmanaged technical debt, fragmented ownership, late-stage controls, and delivery practices that are not fit for AI.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technology Delivery
Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.
AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership
Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.
Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration
Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.
Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery
Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.
Quality, Risk and Responsible AI
Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.
Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership
Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

Key Success Measures

Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

Required Skills And Competencies

Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

Qualifications And Experience

15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.

Leadership Expectations

Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.

new_jobs.title: Director of Pricing & Monetization
new_jobs.description:
About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence, supporting workflows across compliance, advisory, training, tax writing, and more.

Backed by a $176M USD Series E funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

We are excited to meet with qualified candidates and are grateful for everyone's interest. This is a remote position open to candidates anywhere in Canada, with occasional travel to our Toronto office as needed. All candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

To help you get off to a great start, we bring all new team members together for their first three days of onboarding. If you’re based outside of our local commuting area, Blue J will arrange and cover your travel and accommodation.

The Opportunity

Reporting To The VP, GTM Strategy & Operations, The Director Of Pricing & Monetization Will Lead Pricing And Packaging Analysis And Recommendations At Blue J. You'll Explore The Questions That Shape Our Commercial Strategy

Who are our customers, and how do their needs differ?
How do they get value from Blue J, and how should our pricing reflect it?
How should our offering evolve as our product portfolio and customer base expand?

You'll collaborate with Finance, Product, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Revenue Operations, and regularly present recommendations to the executive team.

You'll draw on experience in finance, FP&A, or a related analytical field to turn complex data into clear, actionable recommendations. You'll build models, conduct analysis, and communicate findings to stakeholders with different perspectives and priorities, helping the team reach decisions and bring pricing and packaging changes to market.

What You’ll Be Doing

Pricing & Packaging Strategy

Lead analysis and develop recommendations for Blue J’s pricing and packaging structure, including plans, tiers, bundles, and add-ons.
Evaluate how our pricing model can evolve as we launch new products and capabilities and serve a broader range of customer segments.
Identify value metrics that align what customers pay with the value they receive.
Develop principles and guidelines for discounting, promotions, renewals, and price changes.
Build and maintain a prioritized monetization roadmap in partnership with GTM and Product leadership.

Financial Modeling & Analysis

Build business cases and financial models to assess how pricing and packaging changes affect acquisition, conversion, expansion, retention, and customer lifetime value.
Partner with Finance on revenue forecasting and scenario planning related to pricing decisions.
Analyze deal, usage, and customer data to understand willingness to pay, actual prices paid, and discounting patterns.
Measure the impact of pricing initiatives on annual recurring revenue (ARR) and margins, and share results with leadership.

Customer & Market Insights

Develop segmentation frameworks based on customer needs, behaviours, and willingness to pay.
Conduct qualitative and quantitative research, including customer interviews, surveys, win/loss analysis, and churn analysis, to test pricing assumptions.
Monitor competitive pricing and SaaS and AI monetization trends, identifying developments relevant to Blue J’s strategy.

Experimentation & Implementation

Design pricing and packaging experiments with clear hypotheses, success measures, and safeguards for customer trust and retention.
Collaborate with relevant teams to implement approved changes across configure, price, quote (CPQ) systems, billing, and reporting.
Develop rollout and transition plans for new and existing customers, and provide training and resources for Sales and Customer Success.
Establish post-launch measurement plans and refine approaches based on results and feedback.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication

Establish a regular process for pricing reviews and decisions, with clear responsibilities across Finance, Product, and GTM.
Present recommendations to executive leadership, clearly explaining the supporting evidence, trade-offs, and potential impacts.
Advise Sales and Customer Success leadership on deal structures and pricing questions.

What You Offer Blue J

7+ years of experience in pricing, monetization, FP&A, strategic finance, or revenue strategy, ideally within B2B SaaS.
Experience analyzing, recommending, and implementing pricing or packaging changes.
Deep analytical and financial modeling skills, with a strong command of SaaS metrics and subscription economics (ARR, NRR, churn, CAC, LTV, gross margin).
Experience with a range of pricing models, such as seat-based, usage- or consumption-based, value-based, and hybrid approaches.
Comfort working directly with large datasets; proficiency in SQL and advanced spreadsheet modeling; experience with AI and BI tools.
Ability to communicate findings and recommendations clearly in presentations and written communication, and collaborate with executives and teams across Blue J to reach decisions.
Ability to evaluate commercial decisions by considering customer value, growth, and long-term strategy.
Comfort operating autonomously in a fast-moving, high-growth environment where processes are still being built.
Comfortable leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to drive efficiency, improve workflows, and stay ahead of industry trends.

Nice To Have

Experience supporting AI product monetization or designing and running pricing experiments.
Experience supporting pricing or packaging as a company expands its product portfolio.
Familiarity with configure, price, quote (CPQ) and billing systems.
Experience in pricing consulting, an MBA, a CFA designation, or comparable practical experience.

What We Offer You

A rare opportunity to own the pricing and monetization strategy at a fast-growing, well-funded AI company at a pivotal stage of its growth.
A mission-driven culture where your work directly advances clarity, efficiency, and accessibility in tax research.
Competitive base salary, stock options, and benefits designed to support you and your family.
Flexibility in how you work primarily remote, with occasional travel to our Toronto office and conferences as needed.
A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive team that values innovation, respect, and fun.
The excitement of a fast-growing, well-funded company with clear momentum, and the resources to back bold initiatives.

The Core Values that Define Our Culture

We are customer-focused
We put team over self
We are pleasant and playful
We are open to better ideas
We move fast and fix things

What To Expect In The Interview Process

We anticipate a high volume of applicants for this role and are excited to grow our team. A human will review each application and get back to you as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you!

Interview Process

Chat with Natalie, Sr. TA Manager
Meet Paul H. VP, GTM Strategy & Operations
Meet Christine M. VP, Product Marketing
Present your case study
Meet Ben, our CEO

We believe our strength is built on diversity of thought, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. We value inclusiveness and are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We strive to create an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, please let us know in your application. Our team is dedicated to providing the necessary support and making reasonable adjustments to ensure a smooth process for everyone.

How We Use AI In Our Hiring Process

To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Blue J uses AI-enabled tools within our applicant tracking system to help organize applications and highlight profiles that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions.

Every application is reviewed by a member of our Talent team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans.

We use these tools to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment and we’re committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Compensation

The base pay range for this role is $165,000–$206,500 per year.

This is a Level 6 in Blue J’s career level framework. We use levels to define the expected scope, autonomy, impact, decision-making, and experience for each role. Final compensation will be set fairly and thoughtfully based on experience, expertise, and alignment with the role’s responsibilities. While all candidates are expected to bring directly relevant experience, the top of the range is typically reserved for individuals who demonstrate exceptional depth in the role’s core competencies, a strong track record of impact in similar environments, and the ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy from day one.

new_jobs.title: Associate Director, Actuarial Solutions
new_jobs.description:
Why You’ll Love Working Here

high-performance, people-focused culture
our commitment that equity, diversity, and inclusion are fundamental to our work environment and business success, which helps employees feel valued and empowered to be their authentic selves
learning and development initiatives, including workshops, Speaker Series events and access to LinkedIn Learning, that support employees’ career growth
membership in HOOPP’s world class defined benefit pension plan, which can serve as an important part of your retirement security
competitive, 100% company-paid extended health and dental benefits for permanent employees, including coverage supporting our team's diversity and mental health (e.g., gender affirmation, fertility and drug treatment, psychological support benefits of $2,500 per year, parental leave top-up, and a health spending account).
optional post-retirement health and dental benefits subsidized at 50%
yoga classes, meditation workshops, nutritional consultations, and wellness seminars
the opportunity to make a difference and help take care of those who care for us, by providing a financially secure retirement for Ontario healthcare workers

Job Summary

he Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP) is a defined benefit pension plan serving members and employers in Ontario's healthcare sector. The Pension Services division supports the delivery of HOOPP's pension promise through accurate and reliable service to members and employers.

Reporting to the Director, Actuarial Solutions, the Associate Director provides technical leadership to ensure the accuracy and integrity of pension calculations and pension-related data across HOOPP's administration system, member-facing solutions, and off-system tools.

The Associate Director is a senior resource for pension calculations, pension data, system functionality, testing, defect management, and modernization of calculation capabilities. The role helps ensure that on- and off-system solutions using pension data or calculations are accurate, well controlled, and aligned with HOOPP's administration practices and member service objectives. The Associate Director works with various teams to translate plan provisions, legislation, policy, and administration practices into practical solutions through requirements, testing, implementation, and operational controls.

What You Will Do

Calculation Accuracy and Technical Leadership
Provide leadership to ensure the accuracy of pension calculations and member-facing pension information across HOOPP’s administration system, digital services, and off-system tools.
Act as a senior subject matter expert for complex pension calculations and pension administration concepts, including escalated, precedent-setting, and high-risk cases.
Identify inconsistencies among plan provisions, policy, administration practices, system logic, member communications, and calculation tools, and lead their resolution or escalation.
Advise senior leaders on calculation risks, member impacts, and recommended courses of action while balancing calculation integrity, efficiency, and member experience.
Promote consistent, explainable, and sustainable calculation logic across member-facing solutions.
Cross-Functional Delivery and Strategic Initiatives
Act as the actuarial lead for cross-functional initiatives, coordinating stakeholders, influencing project direction, identifying risks and dependencies, and helping ensure solutions involving pension calculations or pension data are delivered successfully.
Ensure calculation- and data-related considerations are incorporated early in discovery, design, requirements, delivery, testing, and implementation.
Assess proposed solutions for calculation accuracy, appropriate use of data, alignment with plan provisions, and member impact.
Lead or support implementation of plan, legislative, policy, or administration-practice changes affecting calculations or pension data.
Build effective relationships and influence decisions without direct authority, including challenging proposals where calculation integrity may be at risk.
Calculation Requirements, Tools, and Modernization
Lead the development of calculation requirements, implementation planning, testing strategies, and business readiness activities for calculation engine capabilities and other calculation solutions.
Establish standards for and develop calculation requirements, including business intent, formulas, data inputs, dependencies, exception handling, auditability, and outputs.
Ensure requirements are complete, maintainable, and sufficiently detailed for business analysts, developers, and end-users.
Identify and lead opportunities to automate exception processing and recurring activities while maintaining appropriate controls and human oversight.
Set standards for calculation tools and other off-system solutions, including testing, approval, version control, access, monitoring, and change management.
Release Delivery, Testing, and Calculation Quality
Lead the Actuarial Solutions team’s work on calculation-related changes to HOOPP’s pension administration system, from early design and requirements through to testing, implementation, and production monitoring.
Set and execute testing approaches, ensuring they cover regression testing, complex cases, and data storage.
Assess release readiness and ensure identified defects and required controls are documented and escalated.
Coordinate and participate in production validations of calculation functionality, rate tables, and calculation controls after a release is deployed.
Lead the review and resolution of calculation defects and production incidents, including impacted-member analysis, interim controls, correction methods, and validation of fixes.
Act as the point of contact for external vendors and stakeholders as it relates to discussions involving calculations or pension data storage. Lead discussions and find resolutions that prioritize calculation and data accuracy in HOOPP’s pension administration system.
Lead audits of HOOPP’s pension administration system and related tools to ensure consistent quality.
Pension Data and Calculation Controls
Provide oversight for the interpretation and appropriate use of pension administration data in calculations, member-facing solutions, and internal processes.
Ensure the correct data fields and transformations are used where the results could affect pension amounts or related information shown to members, employers, or internal staff.
Define data requirements for initiatives involving pension calculations, reporting, or the presentation of pension information.
Partner with Pension Technology, Product & Delivery Management, Member & Employer Services, and other Pension Services teams to ensure pension data is used consistently and accurately across solutions.
Recommend new pension data health checks, calculation controls, or monitoring activities where issues are identified.
Recommend updates to existing pension data health checks based on changing needs.
Assess and communicate risks arising from pension data quality issues or control gaps.

What You Will Bring

University degree in actuarial science
An ASA or ACIA designation is required; progress towards FCIA designation is preferred
Ten or more years of progressively responsible experience in pensions consulting, actuarial work, pension administration, pension systems, or a related field.
Several years of experience leading complex technical initiatives, establishing standards, making or recommending high-impact technical decisions, and influencing cross-functional project delivery.
Deep knowledge of defined benefit pension administration, pension calculations, applicable legislation, plan provisions, and administrative policy.
Demonstrated ability to interpret complex pension provisions and translate them into clear calculation requirements and business rules.
Experience leading calculation-related system implementations, testing strategies, and defect resolution
Ability to understand, review, and challenge complex system calculations, Excel-based calculation tools, and other off-system calculations.
Ability to communicate complex actuarial and technical matters clearly to various teams and senior leaders.
Strong judgment and decision-making ability where errors could affect member benefits, financial outcomes, regulatory compliance, or member experience.
Demonstrated ability to set technical direction, prioritize competing demands, manage dependencies and risks, and deliver outcomes through influence rather than direct authority.
Demonstrated ability to resolve complex technical issues and influence decisions across various teams and initiatives.
Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence across various teams and leaders.

The expected annual base salary range for this role is: $103,000 - $153,000 CAD

The actual base salary offered to the successful candidate may vary based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, individual's expertise and level of experience applicable to the role they are being offered.

This role is eligible to participate in discretionary incentive plan(s), subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan text.

This job is for an existing vacancy.

At IPEX, the leader in thermoplastic piping systems, we are redefining the future of water management and clean energy. Job Summary

The Director, Enterprise Process & Business Readiness is accountable for leading the business transformation activities required to successfully deploy SAP across the enterprise’s manufacturing and distribution network.

Reporting to the VP, ERP Business Transformation, this role serves as the senior business counterpart to the Director of ERP Delivery and is responsible for ensuring the organization is operationally prepared for the ERP deployment through process standardization, stakeholder alignment, organizational readiness, and deployment governance.

The role partners closely with the Director, ERP Change & Training, Director, Data Governance & Management, Business Process Owners, Functional Leaders, Site Leadership Teams, and IT to drive adoption of standardized SAP-enabled business processes across IPEX’s manufacturing plants and distribution centres.

The Director leads the enterprise-wide efforts to establish consistent operating practices, collaborate in the transformation of operational master data, mobilize business resources, and implement objective readiness measures that ensure successful deployment and business continuity during cutover and go-live.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Process Transformation

Lead enterprise process transformation by establishing the future-state business process model, leveraging SAP standard capabilities, leading practices and simplification opportunities
Dotted line partner with the Business Process Owners (BPOs) to document, sustain, and deploy future-state processes
Establish governance mechanisms to ensure adherence to standardized processes and minimize local customization
Drive alignment between enterprise process standards and site-level operational requirements
Resolve conflicts between local business practices and enterprise process design
Facilitate process harmonization workshops with functional and operational leadership teams
Ensure process design decisions support scalability, compliance, operational efficiency and SAP standard functionality
Own business governance, quality, and stewardship of operational master data across assigned process domains.
Approve and prioritize master data changes, ensuring compliance with data standards, controls, and business requirements.
Partner with Data Governance, Data Stewards, and IT teams to define, maintain, and continuously improve master data processes and controls.

Business Readiness

Develop and execute the enterprise business readiness strategy for ERP deployment
Identify points of failure, risks, business contingency plans, and the metrics that trigger identified contingencies
Develop key tactics to alter timing of typical business rhythms by advancing or deferring core activities or operations
Plan daily operations to compensate for reduced staffing during training period
Develop and deploy operational targets (KPIs), monitoring methods, and reporting cadence
Collaborate on planning staffing levels to compensate for loss of efficiency during Hypercare
Ensure employees understand any role or responsibility changes
Determine key user and backfill needs; outline coverage and working schedule
Support external business partners on key actions and dates to align changes within their operations
Identify operational leader roles for Cutover and Hypercare coverage
Identify leaders responsible for cascading information
Create opportunities to share transparent, timely updates
Identify potential roadblocks to successful transfer to Business ownership
Plan supervisors’ daily activities post-Go Live to support new ways of working and identify issues early
Drive stakeholder engagement across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, customer service, finance and commercial functions
Build commitment and ownership among operational leaders for adopting for adopting new ways of working
Lead readiness reviews with executive stakeholders and deployment governance teams
Partner with Operational Change Management & Training to ensure training, process adoption, organizational readiness, and business ownership are achieved before deployment

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business; MBA considered beneficial
10-15 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, operations, ERP transformation, or operational excellence
Proven experience leading large-scale, multi-year ERP deployments, preferably SAP
Experience deploying standardized business processes across multiple manufacturing locations
Experience establishing operational master data governance and quality programs
Experience influencing senior leaders across operational and functional organizations
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives

Provides independent, objective review and adjudication of credit applications and transactions for an assigned portfolio within credit limits or makes credit recommendations and escalates as required. Ensures the credit quality of the assigned portfolios are maintained within the Bank’s risk tolerance, policies & procedures, and meet financing guidelines. Supports credit adjudication operations and initiatives. Provides training and support to teams and channels where the applications and transactions originate.

Works with stakeholders to ensure effectiveness of risk management controls, analysis and monitoring on a transactional and portfolio basis.
Provides credit coaching, training and support to direct team and other stakeholders as required.
Provides strategic input into business decisions as a trusted advisor.
Makes recommendations to senior leaders on strategy and new initiatives, based on an in-depth understanding of the business/group.
Acts as a subject matter expert on relevant regulations and policies.
May network with industry contacts to gain competitive insights and best practices.
Influences and negotiates to achieve business objectives.
Identifies emerging issues and trends to inform decision-making.

Conducts independent analysis and assessment to resolve strategic issues.
Acts as the prime subject matter expert for internal/external stakeholders.
Ensures alignment between stakeholders.
Develops and manages comprehensive information management systems; designs and/or leads initiatives to improve processes, analysis and reporting.
Integrates information from multiple sources to enable more efficient processes, enhanced analysis and/or streamlined reporting.

Employs systems (e.g. customized exception reports, tracking reports etc.) to manage information.
Breaks down strategic problems, and analyses data and information to provide insights and recommendations.

Leads the development of the communication strategy focusing on positively influencing or changing behaviour.
Collaborates across BMO to develop communications strategies and ensure consistency of messaging, in order to positively influence or change behaviour.
Leads the execution of operational programs; assesses and adapts as needed to ensure quality of execution.
Supports credit due diligence activities for bank acquisitions or integration.
Reviews and communicates decisions on credit transactions with rationale that can be understood and explained to customers.
Identifies and advises on terms, conditions and collateral requirements for the transaction decision as well as opportunities for cross-selling and/or alternative solutions to meet client’s needs.
Keeps abreast of economic and market developments within the portfolio to inform decision making and credit risk policies.
Provides approval for exceptions according to established policy and standards.
Monitors the credit portfolio through transaction review & approval to ensure compliance with the Bank’s lending policies and procedures.
Provides credit risk coaching and advice to sales & service employees to increase awareness of risk, policy, and knowledge of structuring transactions.
Builds effective relationships with internal/external stakeholders.
Gathers and formats data into regular and ad-hoc reports, and dashboards.
Monitors and tracks performance and addresses any issues.
Executes work to deliver timely, accurate, and efficient service.
Operates at a group/enterprise-wide level and serves as a specialist resource to senior leaders and stakeholders.
Applies expertise and thinks creatively to address unique or ambiguous situations and to find solutions to problems that can be complex and non-routine.
Implements changes in response to shifting trends.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.

Typically 7+ years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Credit Qualifications and associated credit knowledge and skills according to the established qualification standards.
In-depth / expert knowledge of banking products & services.
In-depth / expert knowledge of industry trends and regulations.
In-depth / expert knowledge of credit portfolio management policies & procedures, and financing guidelines.
Proven leadership skills and highly developed coaching skills.
Seasoned professional with a combination of education, experience and industry knowledge.
Verbal & written communication skills - In-depth / Expert.
Analytical and problem solving skills - In-depth / Expert.
Influence skills - In-depth / Expert.
Collaboration & team skills; with a focus on cross-group collaboration - In-depth / Expert.
Able to manage ambiguity.
Data driven decision making - In-depth / Expert.

North America Construction (1993) Ltd. – NAC Constructors Ltd. (NAC) is well known for our expertise in water and wastewater construction across Canada. Our self-performing team of almost 500 skilled professionals and experts in trades and engineering, comprehensively handles projects, from conceptualization to delivery. Bring your construction industry knowledge and technology leadership experience to NAC, where you’ll have the opportunity to shape our technology strategy, modernize business systems, and drive meaningful business transformation.

North America Construction (NAC) is looking for a business-minded technology leader who understands the demands of a construction or project-based environment and can translate technology into practical business improvements.

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Services, you will lead NAC’s technology strategy, manage a small internal technology team, and oversee external providers. Working closely with executive leadership and teams across finance, operations, estimating, HR, equipment, and projects, you will improve business systems, decision-making, productivity, and the employee experience.

Position Responsibilities:

Technology Strategy & Governance

Maintain a technology and transformation roadmap aligned with corporate priorities and business objectives.
Establish technology governance, standards, policies and decision-making processes.
Manage budgets and investment plans, assess emerging technologies, and develop and present business cases to executive leadership.

Enterprise Applications

Provide strategic direction for NAC’s enterprise applications, including ERP platforms, Jonas Construction Software, Procore, Primavera P6, Concur, HR systems, equipment and fleet systems, and future applications.
Lead or oversee enterprise system implementations, integrations, modernization and enhancements, including requirements definition, vendor management, implementation planning, change management and user adoption. Data & Analytics

Lead data governance, stewardship, business intelligence and reporting capabilities, including Power BI, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs, and data warehouse and reporting architecture.
Ensure teams have access to reliable, timely and actionable information to support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.

Digital Workplace, Automation & AI

Lead digital workplace strategy, governance, and adoption across Microsoft 365, SharePoint Online, Teams, Power Platform, and Copilot.

Identify opportunities to improve productivity and business efficiency through effective implementation, change management and employee adoption.

Lead initiatives to simplify workflows, reduce manual and administrative effort, and improve productivity and operational effectiveness. Work with business leaders to establish, measure, and evaluate the benefits and outcomes of these initiatives.

Post-secondary degree or diploma in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, Engineering, Information Systems or a related discipline preferred. Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience will be considered.
Relevant professional certifications in project management, business analysis, IT service management, cybersecurity, enterprise architecture or organizational change management are considered assets.
10+ years of progressive experience in technology leadership, business systems, enterprise applications, digital transformation or business technology, with increasing responsibility for strategy, delivery and organizational outcomes.
Demonstrated experience leading technology functions, internal teams, external service providers and enterprise-wide initiatives.
Experience in construction, engineering, infrastructure, manufacturing or other project-based organizations strongly preferred.
Proven experience developing and executing enterprise technology strategies, roadmaps, governance frameworks and investment plans aligned with business objectives.
Demonstrated experience leading ERP implementations, enterprise application modernization, system integrations and business systems optimization.
Strong understanding of enterprise architecture, data management, business intelligence, analytics and executive reporting.

Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise reporting frameworks, executive dashboards, consistent KPIs and data governance practices that support operational, financial and strategic decision-making.
Demonstrated success leading technology-enabled business transformation, process improvement and organizational change initiatives, with a focus on measurable business outcomes.
Experience overseeing IT operations, infrastructure, cybersecurity, technology risk management, business continuity and disaster recovery planning.
Familiarity with AI, automation, Microsoft Copilot and emerging technologies, including their practical business applications, governance considerations and organizational adoption.
Strong business acumen and financial awareness, with the ability to develop business cases, evaluate technology investments and assess their business value.
Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder management and change leadership skills, including the ability to translate complex technology concepts into practical business recommendations and outcomes.

Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls

10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen

Problem solving

Results orientation and a bias for action

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.

Join CPKC, North America’s first transnational railroad connecting U.S., Canada, and Mexico, where your career drives progress and safety is paramount. The Director, Intermodal & Automotive Operations is a key leadership role responsible for driving operational excellence across all aspects of Intermodal and Automotive Operations within an assigned territory. This leader will inspire and develop a high-performing team of CPKC employees, delivering exceptional results in safety, service, asset utilization, cost management, and workforce engagement. Operating in a fast-paced, highly strategic environment, the Director will leverage strong leadership, sound judgment, and a relentless sense of urgency to optimize performance, enhance customer experience, and support the continued growth of the business.

Lead the execution of business strategy and operating plans for Intermodal and Automotive terminals across the assigned territory
Drive daily operational performance by achieving safety, service, productivity, and cost KPI objectives
Serve as the primary escalation point for operational issues impacting network performance, customer service, terminal operations, and commercial objectives
Champion a culture of safety, compliance, accountability, and continuous improvement across all facilities
Optimize terminal fluidity and network efficiency through effective train design, capacity planning, and resource allocation
Develop, coach, and manage leaders through performance management, career development, succession planning, and accountability
Ensure terminal service metrics, including truck dwell and operational efficiency targets, consistently meet customer and business expectations
Manage strategic relationships with contractors and vendors, including contract administration, RFPs, performance management, and resource planning
Oversee facility security, equipment regulatory compliance, and capital planning initiatives to support current and future operational growth

High school diploma General Equivalency required; Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Transportation, Business, or a related field preferred
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in rail transportation, terminal operations, logistics, or a related operational leadership environment
Extensive knowledge of rail operations, including intermodal and automotive terminal environments
Proven leadership experience developing, coaching, and leading diverse unionized, non-union, and contractor workforces
Strong understanding of collective bargaining agreements, labor relations, and applicable employment laws
Valid driver’s license
Valid passport with ability to travel to US without restrictions

Flexible and competitive benefits package

Performance incentive plan

Part-time studies program

Medical and Drug Testing

Criminal history check
Education verification
Professional references
Driver’s license verification and driving history
Passport verification

As an employee with a North American presence, the possibility does exist that the location of your position may be changed based on organizational requirements.

Becoming a qualified conductor or locomotive engineer is the single best way for a management employee to learn the business at CPKC. You may be required to obtain a certification or to maintain your current certification/qualification as a conductor or locomotive engineer.

The Director, Digital & Demand Generation is responsible for driving demand generation, digital marketing performance and pipeline growth across KORE's IoT and connectivity business. The role leads a team covering Digital Advertising, Marketing Operations, Email Marketing, Website and KORE Shop, alongside two Sales Development Representatives (SDRs). The position combines digital marketing strategy, operational delivery and team leadership, with a strong focus on generating qualified sales opportunities and revenue.

Core Accountabilities

Digital Marketing & Demand Generation

Develop and execute KORE's digital marketing and demand generation strategy, focused on generating qualified leads, sales opportunities and pipeline growth.
Manage paid and organic marketing campaigns across search, digital advertising and other relevant channels, ensuring investment delivers measurable commercial results.
Oversee SEO, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) initiatives to improve KORE's visibility across traditional search engines and AI-powered platforms.
Continuously assess campaign targeting, messaging and creative performance to improve lead quality, conversion and return on investment.

Website, KORE Shop & Email Marketing

Own the performance and ongoing development of KORE's website and KORE Shop, improving user experience, conversion rates and online sales.
Oversee email marketing, lead nurturing and marketing automation programs to support prospect engagement and conversion.
Ensure digital channels and content support customer acquisition and wider commercial objectives.

Marketing Operations & Pipeline Performance

Oversee the marketing technology stack, campaign tracking, lead attribution and pipeline reporting.
Establish clear performance measures focused on qualified meetings, sales opportunities, pipeline contribution and revenue rather than activity or engagement metrics alone.
Use marketing and sales data to evaluate campaign effectiveness, identify opportunities for improvement and guide investment decisions.
Work closely with Sales to ensure marketing activities are aligned with commercial priorities and pipeline targets.

SDR Leadership & Team Development

Lead and develop the digital marketing and SDR teams, setting clear objectives, priorities and performance expectations.
Oversee SDR activities, ensuring effective lead qualification, follow-up and conversion into sales meetings and opportunities.
Develop and improve marketing operations and SDR processes to support efficient lead management and pipeline generation.
Build a commercially focused team with clear accountability for delivery and results.

Agency Management & Collaboration

Manage external digital marketing agencies and partners, setting clear performance expectations and holding them accountable for results.
Work closely with Sales, Product and other internal stakeholders to align campaigns, messaging and demand generation activities.
Balance analytical insight with creative judgement to improve campaign effectiveness and commercial outcomes.

Qualifications

Significant experience in digital marketing, demand generation or performance marketing, ideally within IoT, telecommunications, connectivity or B2B technology.
Proven experience developing and delivering digital marketing campaigns that generate qualified leads and sales pipeline.
Strong knowledge of paid search, organic search, SEO and emerging AI-driven search practices, including AEO and GEO.
Experience managing corporate websites, e-commerce platforms and conversion rate optimization.
Strong understanding of email marketing, lead nurturing, marketing automation and CRM platforms, such as Salesforce and HubSpot.
Experience with marketing attribution, analytics, pipeline reporting and performance measurement.
Experience managing and developing marketing or sales development teams.
Strong commercial awareness, analytical skills and the ability to use data to guide decisions and improve results.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with Sales and other business functions.

The Senior Director is a key member of the Parks and Recreation senior leadership team and shares accountability, alongside the General Manager and fellow Senior Directors, for the overall leadership, performance and strategic direction of the division. Operating within a highly collaborative executive environment, the leadership team works collectively to establish priorities, guide decision-making, allocate resources and advance Council-approved objectives. While accountable for their assigned portfolio and serving as the section's lead representative for related Council, committee, media and stakeholder matters, Senior Directors are expected to adopt an enterprise-wide lens, balancing portfolio needs with the broader interests of the division, the City and the communities it serves. Through this collective leadership model, the team drives integrated solutions, organizational excellence and consistent service delivery across Parks and Recreation.

Toronto Parks and Recreation delivers services and spaces that enhance the quality of life for millions of residents. As Toronto continues to grow and evolve, the division must make complex decisions about where and how to invest in parks, recreation facilities and community infrastructure to meet future needs.

The City of Toronto is seeking a strategic and accomplished leader to serve as Senior Director, Capital & Parks Planning.
Reporting to the General Manager, Parks and Recreation, the Senior Director leads a broad portfolio encompassing capital planning, system planning, asset management, growth planning, parkland acquisition and long-term infrastructure investment strategy. Serving as the critical link between planning, capital delivery and operations, this role ensures investment decisions are informed by service realities while positioning Toronto's parks and recreation system for the future.

The decisions made through this portfolio will shape the future of parks, recreation facilities and community infrastructure across Toronto for decades to come. Success requires exceptional strategic judgment, political acuity and the ability to navigate competing priorities, complex stakeholder interests and significant public investments.

Leading through a team of Directors and multidisciplinary professionals, you will integrate planning, capital and asset management functions under a unified strategic framework. You will strengthen connections between long-range planning, capital delivery and operational service needs while advancing the division's asset management maturity and long-term infrastructure priorities.

Working closely with elected officials, senior leaders, Indigenous communities, government agencies, developers, community organizations and residents, you will build consensus, guide complex decisions and advance major initiatives in a highly visible and politically sensitive environment.

What You Bring to the Role:

Post-secondary education in Urban Planning, Engineering, Landscape Architecture, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Extensive senior leadership experience in strategic planning, infrastructure planning, capital investment, asset management, growth management or related portfolios within a large, complex organization.
Extensive experience in either the planning or infrastructure/capital delivery environment, combined with the ability to effectively lead and integrate multidisciplinary teams across both functions.
Demonstrated success developing and implementing long-term infrastructure, growth, service or asset management strategies involving significant stakeholder engagement, competing priorities and complex decision-making.
Experience overseeing large-scale capital investment planning and portfolio prioritization processes, balancing growth, state-of-good-repair and community service objectives.
Proven ability to navigate politically sensitive and highly visible environments requiring diplomacy, judgment, influence and exceptional stakeholder management skills.
Experience building productive partnerships with elected officials, government agencies, developers, Indigenous communities, community organizations and senior executives.
Experience leading senior managers, specialized professionals and multidisciplinary teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and strategic thinking.
Experience presenting complex strategic recommendations, investment priorities and policy matters to senior leadership teams, elected officials, boards and committees.
Familiarity with legislative and regulatory frameworks relevant to municipal planning, infrastructure delivery, asset management and occupational health and safety.
